title: Claude Managed Agents
content:
## Overview

**Claude Managed Agents** is Anthropic's cloud-hosted agent orchestration platform, available through the Claude Platform (platform.claude.com). It allows teams to deploy, configure, and run autonomous Claude agents at scale without managing their own infrastructure. Several significant capabilities were added to the platform in May–June 2026.

---

## Multiagent Orchestration

Managed Agents now supports a **lead agent / specialist subagent** pattern natively:

- A lead agent receives the top-level task and decomposes it into subtasks
- Specialist subagents run **in parallel** on a shared filesystem, each configured with its own model, system prompt, and tool set
- Sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents; **background chains are capped at five levels deep** to prevent runaway recursion
- Every session has one implicit team, and teammates are spawned directly with the `Agent` tool's `name` parameter — no separate setup step needed

This matches the patterns available in Claude Code's Agent SDK but runs in Anthropic's managed infrastructure rather than requiring a self-hosted orchestration layer.

---

## Dreaming (Scheduled Memory Curation)

**Dreaming** is a scheduled background process that runs between agent sessions. It:

1. Reviews transcripts from past agent sessions for the same workspace
2. Surfaces recurring patterns — repeated mistakes, common workflows, team preferences
3. Curates these into the agent's persistent memory store

The effect is that agents improve across runs without manual prompt tuning. A coding agent that repeatedly forgets a project's testing convention, for example, will have that convention pulled into its memory after the next Dreaming cycle.

Dreaming runs on a schedule configured per-workspace and is distinct from within-session extended thinking.

---

## Sandbox with Private MCP Servers

Managed Agents can now operate in **a sandbox you control**, with connections to your private Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers:

- The execution environment (where the agent runs tools) stays within your enterprise network boundary
- The agent connects to internal MCP servers — databases, internal APIs, private GitHub instances — without those servers being exposed to Anthropic's infrastructure
- This addresses the data residency and security requirements that previously blocked enterprise adoption of cloud-hosted agents

The sandbox model means the *orchestration* runs in Anthropic's cloud, but the *tool execution* and *data access* happen inside your perimeter.

---

## Rate Limits API

A new **Rate Limits API** lets administrators programmatically query the rate limits configured for their organization and workspaces. This enables:

- Monitoring current quota utilization without logging into the console
- Building dashboards that alert when a workspace approaches its cap
- Automating workspace provisioning (e.g., spin up a new workspace with pre-configured limits)

---

## Claude Code Integration

Several features announced alongside Managed Agents also landed in Claude Code:

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| Rate limit doubling | Claude Code rate limits doubled for all plans |
| Nested sub-agents | Sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents (5-level cap) |
| `/cd` command | Move working directory mid-session without rebuilding prompt cache |
| `fallbackModel` setting | Configure up to three fallback models tried in order when primary is unavailable |
| Faster `/resume` | Up to 67% faster on sessions with 40MB+ context |

---

## Enhanced Web Search (SEC Filings)

The web search tool available to Managed Agents now returns richer **SEC filing data**, including structured citations from primary filings. This improves the grounding quality for financial research agents, earnings analysis, and due-diligence workflows, reducing the need to manually supply document URLs.

---

## Vision Improvements

Vision resolution across Claude Platform models increased to **2,576 px (~3.75 megapixels)**, up from the previous ceiling. This raises performance on visual acuity benchmarks and improves the agent's ability to read fine-grained text from screenshots, diagrams, and scanned documents.
